dossiers.thesis_summary: Ultragenyx faces a hard, dated FDA decision on UX111 (rebisufligene etisparvovec) for Sanfilippo syndrome type A on 19 September 2026 — 25 days out, unfired, not slipped, and resolving purely on its own regulatory facts. The resubmission was accepted 2 April 2026 after a July 2025 complete response letter that was confined to manufacturing information and facility inspection observations, not to whether the drug works. There is no approved therapy for MPS IIIA anywhere in the world. Approval odds are genuinely good — roughly 75% — and a second rare pediatric disease priority review voucher, worth $150-195M on live comparable sales, comes with it. What has changed since the board wrote this dossier is not the event but what the event is worth. On 19 August the company won its first-ever gene therapy approval (GENGLYCOS, four days ahead of its 23 August action date) and took a voucher in hand, and the stock is worth $0.23 more today than the day before. The market has already run this experiment and paid almost nothing for the answer, which is why the win leg is $28 rather than $30 — and why the $18 "floor" the board carried is a price memory, not a floor, on a balance sheet with negative equity and $1.08B of net debt.
dossiers.kill_risk: The residual capture on approval may be zero, not the +$2.28 I have underwritten. The single load-bearing claim in my thesis is that a 19 September approval is not yet fully in the price. The live record argues the opposite and it argues it twice. On 19-20 August the company delivered a strictly larger surprise than the one still on file — a first-ever gene therapy approval, delivered four days EARLY, carrying a voucher worth $150-195M — and the stock opened $28.39, printed its high at $28.50, and closed $25.32 down 10.8% on 3.84M shares. Two weeks earlier a record quarter produced the identical shape: open $28.48 was the day's high, close $24.93, down 12.5%. In both cases the open was the high. Net durable repricing from the August approval plus the voucher is +$0.23 a share. If the market pays roughly nothing for a delivered approval and a voucher in hand, it may pay roughly nothing for a second, better-telegraphed one, and the whole positive expected value rests on a re-rating the tape has just refused twice at the exact level the target must clear. Secondary and unresolved: the July 2025 letter cited observations from inspections of facilities, plural, and UX111 needs both Ultragenyx's Bedford, MA site and Andelyn Biosciences in Columbus, OH. The August approval validated Bedford. Andelyn is an independent contract manufacturer, separately inspectable, and was not cleared by it — so the manufacturing objection is half-answered, not answered.

This management's most recent Phase 3 pair (setrusumab, Orbit) missed on 29 Dec 2025 and took the stock down more than 40% in one session; the same move from $25.72 is $15.43. There is nothing underneath: shareholders' equity is NEGATIVE $291M, total debt $1,202M, net debt $1,077M, cash and investments $442M (down from $540M in Q1, so ~$98M/quarter burn), and a company in that state would be selling stock into the wreckage. This same regulator litigated SECURE's last major merger in this exact market — the Commissioner proved a substantial lessening of competition in 136 of 143 markets in SECURE/Tervita, the Tribunal ordered divestiture of 29 facilities (2023-03), the Federal Court of Appeal upheld it, and the Supreme Court denied leave (2024-02) — and the Bureau separately challenged GFL's own Terrapure acquisition in 2021. dossiers.thesis_summary: NewAmsterdam is a one-asset company. Obicetrapib is an oral CETP inhibitor with three positive Phase 3 LDL-lowering trials in hand (BROADWAY, BROOKLYN, TANDEM), a CHMP positive opinion dated 23 July 2026, and a European Commission approval decision due in the second half of 2026.
